questions.question: Taking cognizance of the pandemic situation in 2021, the Ministry of Ayush, GoI decided the message of International Day of Yoga 2021 celebration will be:

options.text: Be with Yoga, Be at Home!
Yoga at Home, Yoga with Family!

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Be with Yoga, Be at Home!**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Taking cognizance of the **pandemic situation in 2021**, the **Ministry of Ayush, GoI** decided the message of the** International Day of Yoga 2021 celebration** will be **"Be with Yoga, Be at Home!"**.
 
• Owing to the tireless efforts of** Indian Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi,** the Ministry of Ayush launched the **"Be With Yoga, Be At Home" video campaign** in an effort **to unite the world's citizens when they were at home and to propagate the traditional yoga philosophy** for the benefit of both physical and mental health.
 
• The Ministry of Ayush **promoted traditional Yoga** and encouraged people to get ready for and **participate actively in International Day of Yoga **through the** "Be With Yoga, Be At Home"** video campaign.
 
• The campaign **encouraged engagement on MyGov and a number of social media sites**, including Facebook, Twitter, and Instagram.
 
• The campaign **entailed submitting a video of the participant performing one Yogasana for up to one minute**, along with or without a brief reflection from the participant.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Following its** establishment** at the **UN General Assembly** in **2014**, the** International Day of Yoga** is now observed yearly on** June 21** throughout the world.
 
• 
 
**Yoga** is a **collection of physical, mental, and spiritual exercises** that have their roots in** ancient India**. It is practised majorly to **control and still the mind**.

 
 
• 
 
In his 2014 speech to the UN, **Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi** proposed the date of **June 21** since it is the **longest day of the year in the Northern Hemisphere **and has significant meaning in many cultures.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a capital expenditure?

options.text: Loans and advances by the central government
Expenditure on the acquisition of land

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Subsidies payment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A** subsidy** is a **benefit provided** to a person, company, or institution, typically **by the government**.
 
• It can be either **direct subsidies (like cash payments) or indirect subsidies (such as tax breaks)**.
 
• A **government payment made directly or indirectly** to people or businesses is known as a **subsidy**.
 
• According to **economic theory**, subsidies can be **used to counteract market failures and boost economic efficiency**.
 
• **Loans and advances** by the central government, **expenditures on the acquisition of land**, and **investment in shares** are all **capital expenditures**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Government capital expenditures** are **funds used to develop buildings, machinery, equipment, educational and healthcare facilities**, etc.
 
• It **covers the costs incurred by the government** to **make investments** that will yield earnings or dividends in the future and to **acquire fixed assets** like land. **Repaying a debt is a capital expenditure **because it **reduces obligation** in addition to **creating assets**.
 
• By **enhancing production facilities and increasing operational effectiveness**, capital expenditures that result in the formation of assets are **long-term** in nature and **enable the economy to create income for many years**.
 
• Additionally, it **raises labour force participation, assesses the state of the economy, **and **increases its potential for future growth**.

questions.question: Padma Shri awardee, Gulabo Sapera is a _________ dancer of Rajasthan.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kalbelia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Padma Shri awardee, Gulabo Sapera** is a **Kalbelia dancer** of Rajasthan.
 
• The** Kalbelia** are the** tribe of snake charmers** located at the **Thar Desert in Rajasthan**. 
 
• Both **men and women can perform **the Kalbelia dance, which is an essential component of their culture.
 
• The Kalbelia dance is also known as **"Sapera Dance"** and **"Snake Charmer Dance"**.
 
• Beginning in** 2010**, Rajasthan's Kalbelia dance and songs were added to **UNESCO's representative list of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity**.
 
• At the Kalbelia dance, **men play a variety of traditional instruments as women dance**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A prominent form of** folk dance** in the northern Indian state of Rajasthan is **Bhavai**.
 
• During the Bhavai performance, the **male or female performers balance several earthen pots or brass/metal pitchers** while dancing dexterously, **pirouetting and then swaying with the soles of their feet perched on the top of glass bottles**, on the edge of a sword, on the rim of a brass/metal thali or plate and on the broken glass.
 
• The** Kamar tribes** perform the **Tertali or Terah Taali **traditional dance. **Two or three ladies typically perform it while seated** on the ground.
 
• The** Bhil tribe** performs the** Ghoomar or Ghumar**, a traditional Rajasthani folk dance. The dance is **mostly done by veiled ladies wearing the ghaghara**, which are long, flowing dresses.

questions.question: The region of Ganga Brahmaputra basin lies in ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**10°N to 30°N latitude**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The region of the **Ganga Brahmaputra Basin** lies in **10°N to 30°N latitude**.
 
• The Ganga Brahmaputra Basin is located in the** subtropical regions** of the** Indian subcontinent**.
 
• The **Ganga Brahmaputra Basin** is the basin created by the** Ganga and Brahmaputra rivers and their tributaries**.
 
• 
 
The** key characteristics** of this basin are its **rich plains, the Himalayas, and the Sunderbans delta**.

 
 
• 
 
The annual monsoon season, which brings rain from **June to September**, replenishes this area as well with its **torrential downpours**. 

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• 
 
A **river basin** is a** geographical region that is drained by a river and its tributaries**. Eventually, the water that has been drained **produces a bay, river, lake, or any other form of water body**.

 
 
• 
 
For the **purposes of developing and planning for water resources**, **river basins** are considered to be the **primary hydrological unit**.

 
 
• 
 
There are **12 primary river basins** and they are, the **Brahmaputra River Basin, Ganga River Basin, Cauvery River Basin, Indus River Basin, Krishna River Basin, Godavari River Basin, Mandovizuari River Basin, Mahanadi River Basin, Narmada River Basin, Tapi River Basin, Mahi River Basin, and Pamba River Basin**.

 
 
• 
 
The **catchment area of each river** is at least **20,000 square km** and the catchment area for these** rivers as a whole** is **25.3 lakh square km**.

questions.question: Abhinav Bharat Society was a secret society of revolutionaries. It was established in ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bombay Presidency**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Abhinav Bharat Society **was established in the** Bombay Presidency**.
 
• **Vinayak Damodar Savarkar and his brother Ganesh Damodar Savarkar **created the **secret Indian Independence organisation** known as the **Abhinav Bharat Society (Young India Society) **in** 1904**.
 
• When Vinayak Savarkar was still a student at **Fergusson College in Pune**, it was first established at** Nasik **as the** "Mitra Mela"**.
 
• The organisation then **expanded to several hundred revolutionaries and political activist**s, with branches in different **regions of India and also to London **when Savarkar travelled to London to study law.
 
• Following a few **assassinations of British officials** by the Abhinav Bharat Society, the **Savarkar brothers were found guilty and sentenced** to prison, and the organisation was **declared disbanded in 1952**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Calcutta's development as a Presidency city** began in **1699** by the East India Company. In** 1715**, the British finished constructing the **Old Fort**, and in **1717, the Mughal emperor Farrukh-siyar** granted the **East India Company freedom of trade in exchange for a 3,000 rupee yearly payment**.
 
• The** United Provinces of British India**, also referred to simply as the **United Provinces**, was a British Indian province that was created on **January 3, 1921**, as a result of the renaming of the **United Provinces of Agra and Oudh**.
 
• **Punjab Province** was a British Raj province in colonial India, with **Lahore serving as its capital**. Following the **Second Anglo-Sikh War**, the British East India Company designated much of the Punjab region a province under **British Colonial Authority in April 1849**.

questions.question: The British physicist named Paul Dirac was known to have introduced the concept of ______ in 1930.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**antiparticle**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **British physicist** named** Paul Dirac** was known to have introduced the concept of **antiparticle **in** 1930**.
 
• The** antiparticle** is a **subatomic particle that has the same mass as an ordinary matter particle but an opposing electric charge and magnetic moment**.
 
• For example, the **negatively charged electron's antiparticle is the positron**, which has a positive charge.
 
• **Paul Dirac** asserted that **all matter has an antimatter**-like counterpart when he was formulating the **quantum mechanical theory**. If a particle is charged, it and its antiparticle should have **opposing charges**.
 
• **Carl Anderson** identified a positively charged particle in **1932 **by examining the **cosmic ray particle trails in a cloud chamber**. This particle appeared to have an **electron-like mass**.
 
• **Anderson's particle**, which was given the name **"positron"**, was the **first antiparticle** to be experimentally proved.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Atoms **are desorbed from a hot surface through a physical process called** thermal ionisation**, sometimes referred to as **surface ionisation or contact ionisation**, which results in the** creation of ions**.
 
• **High-energy charged particles, x-rays, and gamma rays **are all components of **cosmic radiation**, which stars create. The earth receives **secondary radiation** that is created when charged particles interact with the atmosphere.
 
• The **nuclear model** is a term that refers to** Rutherford's atomic model**. The **protons and neutrons**, which make up almost all of the **mass of the nuclear atom**, are found in the **nucleus, which lies at the centre of the atom**. Since they **surround the nucleus**, the **electrons** take up the majority of the **atom's volume**.

questions.question: Which special order of the courts means “arrested person should be presented before the court"?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Habeas corpus**__.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **special order of the courts, Habeas corpus**, means **“arrested person should be presented before the court"**.
 
• **Habeas corpus** is a legal remedy that **allows a person to inform a court about an illegitimate arrest or imprisonment** and ask that the court compel the person's custodian—typically a prison official—to bring the prisoner to court so that the validity of the arrest can be determined.
 
• **William Blackstone **referred to the **writ of habeas corpus** as a** "great and efficient writ in all manner of illrgal confinement"**.
 
• **Habeas corpus** is a summons that has the** same legal effect as a court order**; it is** directed to the custodian and requests that a prisoner be brought before the court together with documentation of the custodian's authority** so that the court can evaluate if the custodian has the right to hold the prisoner

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• .A **judicial remedy **known as a **mandamus** is an** order from a court to any government, subordinate court, corporation, or public authority** directing them to perform (or refrain from performing) a particular act that they are legally required to perform (or refrain from performing), and which is in the nature of a public duty and, in some cases, a **statutory duty**.
 
• **Certiorari** is a legal procedure **used to ask for judicial review of a ruling made by a lower court or government** **body**.
 
• A writ of prerogative known as a **quo warranto demands that the person to whom it is addressed provide proof of their legal capacity** to exercise a right, power, or franchise.

questions.question: A judge of the Supreme Court can be removed only on the grounds of ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**proven misbehaviour or incapacity**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **judge of the Supreme Court **can be** removed only on the grounds of proven misbehaviour or incapacity**.
 
• An **order of the President must be passed** after an address in **each House of Parliament,** **supported by a majority of the members present and voting and by a majority of not less than two-thirds of those present and voting, and presented to the President in the same Session** for such removal on the ground of such proven misbehavior or incapacity.
 
• Otherwise, a judge of the Supreme Court cannot be removed from office. The **practice of law in any court **or before any other body in India** is prohibited for anyone who has served as a judge of the Supreme Court.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• ​The **process for removal judges is outlined in Article 124(4)** of the Indian Constitution. The **President must issue an order** before removing a **Supreme Court Judge** from office.
 
• The **consent of both Houses of Parliament is required** for such an order. It needs a particular majority of the members who are present and voting within the same session.
 
• The **criteria for **removal a**re proven misconduct or incompetence**. After giving notice to the **Speaker or Chairman of the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha**, respectively, it comes to light.
 
• A **three-judge panel conducts a thorough examination**. They **present the report during the following joint session** of both Houses of Parliament.

questions.question: Which of the following is the first ‘smoke-free state’ in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Himachal Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Himachal Pradesh** is the **first "smoke-free state" in India**, and this historic achievement was made possible by the** effective execution of the "Himachal Grihini Suvidha Scheme" of the Himachal Pradesh government and the "Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana" (PMUY)** of the Central Government.
 
• The programme, which **aimed to provide 8 crores deposit-free LPG connections to low-income households**, was introduced by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi on May 1, 2016,** starting in the Uttar Pradesh district of Ballia. The goal was reached in September 2019.
 
• On **August 10, 2021, Ujjwala 2.0 **was launched on a **pan-India basis **to install another **one crore LPG connections** and cover the remaining homes covered by PMUY.
 
• A crore LPG connections under **Ujjwala 2.0 **have been provided as of **January 31, 2022, **exceeding the government's goal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• India's** first "Carbon Neutral Panchayat"** is **Palli in Jammu & Kashmir**.
 
• Due to the successful execution of the **"Himachal Grihini Suvidha Scheme" **of the Himachal Pradesh Government and the **"Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana (PMUY)"** of the Central Government, **Himachal Pradesh is the first "smoke-free state" **in India.
 
• **Diu is the first Union Territory of India to use only solar energy**. In just three years, the Union Territory (UT) of **Diu has become the first renewable energy surplus region in the entire country**.
 
• **Goa** has succeeded in **providing 100% Functional Home Tap Connections (FHTCs) in rural areas**, making it the** first "Har Ghar Jal" state** in the nation.

questions.question: What is the distance of the penalty mark from the midpoint of the goal post in football?

questions.question: Which of the following type of house remains were found in Mehrgarh site of Harappan civilization?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Square or rectangular**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Square or rectangular** type of **house remains** were found in** Mehrgarh site of Harappan civilization**.
 
• In the **Kacchi Plain in Balochistan, Pakistan**, is the **Neolithic archaeological site** known as **Mehrgarh**.
 
• Early occupants of Mehrgarh** built their square or rectangular homes out of local mud, kept their grain in granaries**, made their own tools out of copper ore found nearby, and lined their big baskets with bitumen.
 
• In addition to **raising sheep, goats, and cattle**, they also **grew dates, jujubes, einkorn wheat, and six-row barley**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Indus Valley Civilization**, commonly referred to as the **Indus Civilization**, was a** Bronze Age civilization in the northwest of South Asia **that flourished between **2600 and 1900 BCE** and was active from** 3300 to 1300 BCE**.
 
• The Indus Civilization is **frequently referred to as Harappan** after its** type site Harappa**, which was the **first to be discovered and excavated** in what was then the **Punjab province of British India and is now Punjab, Pakistan**, early in the 20th century.
 
• The **Early Harappan and Late Harappan cultures **existed side by side in the same region.
 
• **Neolithic cultures**, of which **Mehrgarh in Balochistan, Pakistan, is the oldest and best-known**, were the source of the **early Harappan cultures**. To set the **Harappan Civilization **apart from the older ones, it is frequently referred to as **Mature Harappan**.

questions.question: In 1893, which Swiss chemist was the first to understand the molecular structures of inorganic substances – chemical compounds that do not contain carbon?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** **__**Alfred Werner**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **1893**, the **Swiss chemist, Alfred Werner**, was the **first to understand the molecular structures of inorganic substances** – chemical compounds that do not contain carbon.
 
• Werner asserts that the **attraction forces come uniformly from the centre of the atom** rather than being associated with any particular directions in the atom. He clarified the structures of substances by **assigning a new coordination number** to an atom's bonds.
 
• The** octahedral structure of transition metal complexes** was proposed by** Alfred Werner**, who was **awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1913**.
 
• **Modern coordination chemistry's foundation** was created by Werner and he was the **first to receive the Nobel prize for inorganic chemistry**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **William Ramsay**, who won the **1904 Nobel Prize in Chemistry**, contributed to the **creation of the noble gases as a new group in the periodic table**.
 
• In **1943, George de Hevesy**, a radiochemist from Hungary, won the** Nobel Prize in Chemistry** for discovering the **radiotracer concept**.
 
• **John Dalton **was an English chemist, physicist, and meteorologist best known for **his work on human optics and for introducing the atomic theory to chemistry**.

questions.question: ______ gas is used for the manufacturing of bleaching powder.
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Calcium hypochlorite** is the chemical term for** bleaching powder** and its **chemical formula** is CaOCl₂ .
 
• **Bleaching powder **is a **pale yellowish powder that dissolves in water **and has a** strong chlorine odour**.
 
• **Chlorine gas, which is a byproduct of the chlor-alkali process, reacts with dry slaked lime** to create bleaching powder.
 
• Thus, **chlorine gas** is used for the **manufacturing of bleaching powder**.
 
• Bleaching powder has its applications as a **bleaching agent, oxidizing agent, and disinfectant**.

questions.question: Which of the following dance forms is associated with the state of Himachal Pradesh?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dhaman**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The dance form, **Dhaman** is associated with the state of **Himachal Pradesh**.
 
• The **Nati dance** is unique to the **Sirmaur, Kullu, and Shimla areas of Himachal Pradesh**. The dance was the "most people attending and participating in a Nati dance session at a single place," according to Guinness World Records.
 
• **Himachal Pradesh** also features additional** dance styles** as **Kinnauri, Thoda, Jhora**, Jhali, Chharhi, **Dhaman,** Chhapeli, Mahasu, Dangi, Chamba, Thali, **Jhainta, Daf, and Stick dance**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• One of the most well-known dance styles from** Jammu & Kashmir **is rauf. During **Ramzan and Eid **in the spring, women perform **rauf dance**.
 
• A prominent dancing style among the tribes living in **Jharkhand and the neighbouring state of Bihar** is **phagua** and is performed during the festival of **Holi**.
 
• **Maharashtra and Goa** are known for their renowned folk dance known as **Koli Dance** created by the** Kolis of Mumbai**. All of the **Koli festivals **are always celebrated with **Koli dance**, which r**eflects the rhythm of the ocean waves**.

questions.question: In which of the following groups, are all plants monoecious?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Maize, Cucumber, Fig and Melon**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Plants having both the male and female reproductive parts present** are called **monoecious plants**.
 
• All **gametes, male and female**, are produced by** monoecious plants**.** Androecium**, which refers to the male portion, is **made up of stamens**, and **gynoecium**, which refers to the female portion, is **made up of the pistil**.
 
• Some **examples** of monoecious plants are **Maize, Cucumber, Chara, Fig, Melon, and Coconut.**
 
• It's commonly known as a **hermaphrodite or bisexual flower** when a **flower possesses both male and female reproductive organs.**
 
• It's known as **unisexual** when a **flower just has male or female reproductive organs**. Both staminate and pistillate flowers can be found on a single plant in a **monoecious species**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Dioecious Plant:
 
 
• Dioecious plants refers to plants that have male and female reproductive parts on different plants.
 
• A **dioecious plant** is one that has **either female or exclusively male reproductive organs** **in its flowers.**
 
• Because they **only have one sex organ**, dioecious plants are** referred to as imperfect flowers**.
 
• Examples:
 
 
• **papaya, willow, date palm, poplar, etc**.

questions.question: The annual growth rate percentage population in India gradually started declining in the year _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1981**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **annual growth rate percentage population in India** gradually** started declining in the year 1981**.
 
• ​India has **raised the average marriage age, improved women's access to education**, and enhanced their **quality of life**. As a result, the birth rate has decreased since **1981**.
 
• Other factors that influenced the declining birth rate are **implementation of family planning program**, awareness and knowledge of the **benefits of nuclear family,** and **increasing literacy rate **among states.
 
• **India's growth rate is very rapid **despite a decline in its population. India's population increased dramatically between **1951 and 1981**.
 
• The years from **1921 to 1951 are referred to as the period of stable population growth** in India. This is brought on by** decreased death rates and enhanced sanitation and healthcare **systems.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Increases in a population's or a dispersed group's size** are known as **population growth**. In reality, there is a **1.1% annual increase in the number of people **on earth, or about** 83 million **people.
 
• Because **natural resources are overused **for human progress,** population growth and rising consumption are major contributors to environmental problems including biodiversity loss and climate change**.
 
• The** Sustainable Development Goals**, which **aim to raise living standards globally, lessen society's negative effects on the environment, and promote human welfare**, are the **main focus of international policy aimed at lessening the effects of human population expansion**.
